Subject: Post-demo security handoff: SIG prefill and clarifying items

Hi Janelle / Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great conversation and appreciate the clear operating constraints on data residency and auditability. Per our agreed next steps, I’m starting the security handoff so your security team can kick off the SIG/CAIQ prefill. Attached is our small prefill template that maps to the typical SIG sections — if you can prefill the areas you own and return, we’ll complete the vendor-side answers and then route for any evidence requests.

Quick recap / asks: 
- PulseHealth indicated production data will be US-only (no EU/PAC storage). Please confirm the AWS account/region you plan to use.
- SOC 2: you mentioned an in-house SOC 2 report. If you can share a redacted copy that will speed the process — we treat these as confidential.
- We have two technical clarifications from your security checklist: encryption-at-rest for backups, and the flow for API telemetry/logs (what is sent to PulseHealth vs what we retain).

Timeline: if you can return the prefill + SOC2 PDF by EOD Thu (4/13), we can complete our side and pass to your compliance team for a single consolidated review next week.

Attachments included: 
- SIG_prefill_template.xlsx (attached) — please fill the yellow fields; it aligns with the standard SIGv2 mapping.

If easier, happy to schedule a quick 20-min follow-up with Karthik (cc’d) — he can answer technical questions directly.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-demo security handoff: SIG prefill and clarifying items

Hi all —

Quick answers for the prefill: 
- Telemetry/data retention: Redwood’s runtime forwards aggregate usage metrics and anonymized request metadata (request timestamp, token counts, model id, and anonymized error codes). We do NOT forward prompt text or user-submitted content to PulseHealth or any external partner. Any internal debug logs that may contain partial output are stored in an encrypted internal bucket and are only accessed under strict support procedures; we will document retention periods in the SIG response (30 days for debug logs by default, configurable in Dedicated/Private).
- Backup encryption: Redwood-managed backups are encrypted at rest using customer-tenant-specific AWS KMS CMKs with key rotation every 90 days; access to keys is limited to the platform encryption team. For customers in Dedicated/Private deployments, we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS).
- Evidence: I’ve attached a short architecture diagram and the path to the internal runbook that maps log collection points.

If that covers it I’ll mark the corresponding SIG rows as: 
  - Telemetry: NO (no prompt/user content forwarded); details in comments.
  - Backup encryption: YES (KMS CMK, AES-256, rotation 90d)

Jordan / Marissa — happy to hop on if PulseHealth wants a 20-min tech sync.

-karthik
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
